name: aura
title: Aura
description: A raymarched field of glowing, winding light lines in one WebGL 2 shader: a spectral fan rising from a point, with tint, speed and exposure props.
author: Sabo Sugi <https://codepen.io/sabosugi>
docs:
Installed `Aura` in `components/ui/`, plus the `render-loop` helper in `lib/`. Render `<Aura className="rounded-lg" />`: a 16:9 stage whose background is `--aura-background` (black). Give it a height with `className="aspect-auto h-96"` or lay it behind content with `absolute inset-0`; the picture scales with the box.

The tint multiplies the light (`tint="#7fe3ff"`), `exposure` brightens it (lower values), `speed` and `playing` control the motion, and `time={12}` shows one frame. The shader is analytic (no textures); it draws at a pixel ratio of exactly 1 as the original does (raise `dpr` for crisper lines at a higher cost), pauses off screen and in hidden tabs, shows a still frame under reduced motion and a CSS picture without WebGL 2.

Ported from Sabo Sugi's Aura pen (MIT, copyright 2026 Sabo Sugi): the shader is the pen's, unchanged, drawn with WebGL 2 directly instead of three.js, with the debug panel left out and its starting values as the defaults; the license text is in the file.
